body:
Real milestone, complete result: the calibration run finished. All the way through -- Phase 1 to Phase 6, no hang, no truncation, no time-budget cutoff. First time that has ever happened in this project's recorded history.

The verdict: STAND DOWN. Diagnosed itself as overfit -- train 28.6%, out-of-sample 0.0%, 3 of 6 gates passed. It correctly refused to arm or trade on that result. Zero demo trades placed. That's the safety system doing exactly its job -- finding a real result, recognizing it wasn't trustworthy, and declining to act on it, rather than either hanging (like every prior attempt) or falsely arming.

The honest consequence: because it placed zero trades, the export bridge I built earlier tonight still has nothing in it. So the research-layer tools are built, tested, and correctly still waiting -- this run answered a real question (does USDCHF H1 show a real edge to THIS calibration approach, right now -- no) but it didn't produce the trade-level data the later ship-order steps need. The EA's own log says to recalibrate after market open; it's still running and may try again on fresh data. Never touched the source, the whole way through.

This is a good outcome to end this stretch on, honestly: real infrastructure, run under real conditions, for the first time, worked correctly -- calibration completed, the stand-down logic held, the ratchet log got its first genuinely honest (not falsely-promising) real entry. That's worth more than a lucky trade would have been.

Ledger and status file are current (pass_167). Still watching in case it recalibrates again.
